answer: Each epoch a randomness beacon picks a random sample of agents for a live audit - like cracking a walnut to check the kernel, not the shell. A chosen agent has minutes to solve a puzzle bound to its unique hardware fingerprint and prove it controls one distinct device. Each pass leaves a pigment-like trace in its reputation record; failing, or two answers from one device, flags the cluster. An attacker with a thousand Sybils must keep every fake awake and responsive at unpredictable moments, so cost scales with each fake, while honest agents pay one quick check per epoch.
